steps.title: Wet and green
steps.body: North-west Spain, Galicia and the Basque Country, is Atlantic, with rainfall over 1,500 mm a year in places. It's called green Spain. Vines are often trained high on granite pergolas, called parras, to keep grapes away from damp ground. Wines are fresh, light and aromatic.

steps.title: Rías Baixas
steps.body: Rías Baixas, on Galicia's coast, is built on Albariño, about 96% of plantings. Thick skins resist mildew. The wines have peach, citrus and a saline edge, usually unoaked. There are five sub-zones, including Val do Salnés, the coolest and wettest, and O Rosal, along the Miño river border with Portugal.

steps.prompt: Why is Albariño well suited to Rías Baixas?
options: Its thick skins resist mildew in the damp climate
steps.explanation: Thick skins protect against rot and mildew in one of Spain's wettest regions.

steps.title: Other wines
steps.body: Ribeira Sacra grows Mencía on steep, terraced slopes above the Sil river, giving fresh, floral reds. Valdeorras makes Godello, a textured, mineral white. In the Basque Country, Txakoli is a light, slightly sparkling white from Hondarrabi Zuri, traditionally poured from a height.

steps.prompt: Which wines come from green Spain?
steps.explanation: Priorat is in Catalonia, in the dry north-east.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Green Spain is wet and Atlantic, with high-trained vines
Rías Baixas is built on thick-skinned Albariño
Mencía, Godello and Txakoli complete the north-west
